before_card.label: Shogi
before_card.learning_takeaway: Explain the piece-reuse feature of shogi through a directly supported broad-game overview, leaving the perpetual-check exception to its separate rule card.
before_card.card: Shogi is Japanese chess with a distinctive form of piece reuse. Captured pieces become reserves for their captor. Instead of moving a piece already on the board, a player can spend a turn returning a captured piece to play on their own side.
before_card.original_description: Exploring Japanese chess and its distinctive piece-reuse strategies.

evidence.locator: PDF pages 1, 3 and 12, Comparisons and Placing Captured Pieces
evidence.note: Captured pieces become the captor’s reserves and may be returned to play instead of moving a board piece; no unrestricted-drop or automatic-promotion claim is used.

relations.note: The guide explicitly compares shogi with European chess and identifies returning captured pieces as a difference.
